dedupe_keys.name: gnu radio open source software radio toolkit including digital tv transmitters gr dtv gr atsc3

description: GNU Radio is a free and open-source software development toolkit of signal processing blocks for building software-defined radios. It runs with low-cost external radio hardware or entirely in software as a simulation environment, and is widely used in research, industry, academia, government and by hobbyists. Flowgraphs are built in the graphical GNU Radio Companion or in Python and C++, from blocks for filters, modulation, channel coding and channel models. For broadcasting it includes the gr-dtv component, which absorbed Ron Economos's gr-dvbt2 transmitter in release 3.7.7 and provides ATSC, DVB-T, DVB-T2 and DVB-S2 blocks; gr-dvbt2 implements ETSI EN 302 755 and was verified against BBC test streams. His separate out-of-tree module gr-atsc3 implements an ATSC 3.0 transmitter to the A/322 and A/321 standards, verified against the ATSC validation suite, with Transport Stream input only. Coverage: any standard that can be implemented in software. Format and access: source code and packages, free under GPL v3, with documentation, tutorials and an annual conference. Caveats: a toolkit, not a planning tool; building realistic systems needs signal processing expertise, and over-the-air transmission requires licences. Simulation uses: modelling broadcast and radio links at signal level, testing interference, jamming and receiver behaviour, and training on radio systems. Related records: GNSS-SDR builds on GNU Radio for satellite navigation receivers, and the RF planning suites cover network coverage.
